## The update got a real error message, and a way out of it

**Fixed: tapping "Install update" did nothing.** The app caught every failure from
the Android installer and reported success, so the dialog closed and the app
stayed on the old version. It now:

- keeps the dialog open and tells you **what actually failed** — the file, the
  share permission, or the installer itself;
- opens your **browser** on the download page when the in-app installer can't be
  used, instead of quietly doing nothing (the old fallback called a function a
  web view doesn't have).

**Fixed: "Could not reach the release feed — HTTP 504".** The feed URL was an
alias that redirects, and GitHub's edge was timing out on it. The app now reads
the file directly from the repository (no redirect) and only falls back to the
alias.

## One manual install this time

Your phone is on 2.7.0, whose install button is the broken one, so it can't fetch
this build by itself:

**[Elbiko_Android.apk](https://github.com/C1apot/elbiko-app/releases/latest/download/Elbiko_Android.apk)** —
install it once. From 2.7.3 onward, updates come from inside the app, and if one
ever fails again it will say why and hand you the download page.
